channel.title: ASF Jira
channel.description: This file is an XML representation of an issue

item.title: [IGNITE-1171] Getting affinity for topology version earlier than affinity is calculated
item.description:
During concurrent starting of nodes and cache put/get operations exception occures. Moreover some threads blocked on waiting for futures completion.

CacheAffEarlySelfTest.java for problem reproducing. Note, that exception reproduces not always.

It's important that each node invokes getOrCreateCache() during concurrent start up. It seems when there are concurrent attempts to start the same cache minor topology version differs for different nodes.

item.summary: Getting affinity for topology version earlier than affinity is calculated

status.description: The issue is considered finished, the resolution is correct. Issues which are not closed can be reopened.

comments.comment:
Andrey,

I have several questions about this test:

  1. Is there a good reason why GridCacheffEarlySelfTest.java is attached here?
  2. Can this test be changed, just so we can make it a part of the Ignite test suite? Not doing so will not provide us with any assurance that future changes will not cause the same error again.

Dmitry,

1. I think this test usefull only for problem demonstartion
2. This test doesn't reproduce problem with 100% probability, so it doesn't make sense to include this test to some test suite. Unfortunatelly I have no idea how to change this test in order to reach 100% of reproducing probability.
Andrey, in your test can you plug in your own affinity implementation which will do proper waits in order to reproduce this issue 100% of the time?
I think further investigation needed to create such test you talk about which can be done by the one who will be fixing the issue.
I think further investigation needed to create such test you talk about which can be done by the one who will be fixing the issue.

Test still reproduces (executed on ignite-1.4 branch). See the following files:

  • ignite-1171.20150916.log
  • thread_dump.20150916.1.txt
  • thread_dump.20150916.2.txt

CacheAffEarlySelfTest.java was updated in order to print additional debug info and thread dump when operation hangs.

Note that "Getting affinity for topology version earlier than affinity is calculated" doesn't print in log now. Test just hangs.

Test added to ignite-1171-test branch and reproduces on TC (see http://204.14.53.153/viewLog.html?buildId=66686&buildTypeId=Ignite_IgniteBasic&tab=buildLog)

Currently discovery data is collected on NodeAddedMessage, this leads to the following race:

Nodes 0-6 are in topology, node 7 is joining the grid. At the same time node 0 is attempting to start a cache "A". Node 0 first processes NodeAddedMessage and collects discovery data for node 7, the result is empty. Then node 0 processes custom event which starts the cache. Then node 7 sends NodeAddFinished message and joins the grid. Node 0 sees events [collect, custom, node7 join]. Node 7 receives empty data and no cache is started.

Recent changes in the branch show that generally approach works - custom messages should not be fired in between of NodeAddedMessage and NodeAddFinishedMessage.

However, the changes led to the following issues:

  • Assertion "topology version has not been updated". Caused by sending discard message for custom messages. Now since we re-arrange custom messages, discardId gets repositioned and messages that should have been discarded were not discarded. Fixed the issue above by introducing separate pending queue for custom messages which gets discarded independently from other discovery messages.
  • Assertion "joining nodes is not empty". Did not get to the bottom of the assertion. Coordinator always fires the message at the correct moment, however for some reason custom messages get re-sent after processing and got received by non-coordinator node in the middle of node join process.

I reviewed the final changes in the branch. Looks good to me. TC is green.

Merged to ignite-1.4
